title: Average Ride Time Between Stations
statement:
A metro system records card taps. Build a class that answers how long trips take on average between two stations.

  • TransitLog() creates an empty log.
  • tapIn(id, station, t): rider id enters at station at time t. A rider is in at most one trip at a time.
  • tapOut(id, station, t): rider id leaves at station at time t. It always matches that rider's open tapIn, and t is later than the tap-in time.
  • averageTime(from, to) returns the mean duration of all completed trips that started at from and ended at to. Direction matters: trips from to to from are a different route. At least one such trip exists when it is asked.

The same rider can make many trips over time. Answers within 10⁻⁵ of the exact mean are accepted.

Tests are a list of operations and their arguments; the first creates the log. The expected output has one entry per operation (null where nothing is returned).

examples.out: [null, null, null, null, null, 12.5, null, null, 4, 12.5]
examples.why: Mill → Dock trips took 10 and 15, so the mean is 12.5. Rider 1's return trip, Dock → Mill in 4, is a separate route and does not change the Mill → Dock mean.
The same rider makes two trips of 4 and 7. Both count.

hints: Split the problem in two: trips in progress, and finished trips per route.
Trips in progress: a map from rider id to where and when they tapped in.
Finished trips: you never need the individual durations, only their sum and count per route. Keep those two numbers in a map keyed by the (from, to) pair.

explain.intuition:
An average only needs a running sum and a count. So you never store individual trips. One map holds open trips by rider id: id → (station, time). When a rider taps out, you look up their open trip, compute the duration, and add it to the totals of that route. A second map holds those totals: (from, to) → (sum, count).

It is the same pattern as a metrics collector in a frontend app: you rarely keep every timing sample, just the totals per key, so the dashboard query is O(1).
steps: Keep open: Map<id, [station, t]> and totals: Map<routeKey, [sum, count]>.
tapIn: store [station, t] under the rider's id.
tapOut: read and delete the rider's open entry, build the key from start and end station, and add t − startTime to its sum and 1 to its count.
pitfalls: Building the route key as plain concatenation, like from + to. Then "AB" + "C" and "A" + "BC" collide. Use a separator that cannot appear in a name, or a nested map.
Keying finished trips by rider id. The same rider can repeat a route, and different riders share a route.
Treating A → B and B → A as the same route.

complexity.time: O(1) average per call (plus the key length)

solutions.title: Store every trip
solutions.idea: Keep a list of all finished trips and scan it on each average query.

solutions.title: Running sum and count per route
solutions.idea: Open trips live in one map; each route keeps only a total duration and a trip count.

followups: Report the median trip time per route instead of the mean. What do you have to store now?
Only trips from the last hour should count. How do you expire old ones?
